name: Femoroacetabular Impingement Syndrome
definition: Clinical syndrome of hip-related pain, positive clinical findings and characteristic cam and/or pincer morphology; morphology alone does not equal symptomatic FAI.

typical: Pain with sitting, squatting or sport

investigations.principle: Diagnosis requires symptom, examination and imaging correlation.
investigations.MRI: MRI/MR arthrogram assesses labrum/cartilage where needed.
investigations.radiographs: AP pelvis and lateral hip radiographs assess morphology.

amber: Arthroscopic surgery is considered for persistent appropriate cases after nonoperative care.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Vankshana/Shroni pain phenotype may be documented descriptively.

patientEducation.summary: Clinical syndrome of hip-related pain, positive clinical findings and characteristic cam and/or pincer morphology; morphology alone does not equal symptomatic FAI.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise, locked joint or other listed red flags.
